p1.text: The original star is missing; its current location remains unknown.

p2.text: The rehearsal finishes before the caretaker locks the hall.

p3.text: The moon scene looks as beautiful as the painted scenery.

p4.text: The final scene goes perfectly without anyone noticing Lila.

p5.text: Mouse gives the star to the Moon in the play.

p6.text: The fictional Moon was lonely before receiving a gift.

p7.text: The original star was last seen on the windowsill at lunch, according to Lila.

p8.text: The original star’s loop is repaired.

p9.text: The class is expected in five minutes.

p10.text: The group could skip the final scene.

p11.text: Lila claims skipping the scene will not matter.

p12.text: Ben insists the ending should resolve the Moon loneliness.

p13.text: The sewing kit is in Rowan’s costume cupboard.

p14.text: Return the sewing tin with the needle to Rowan.

p15.text: Do not cut the curtain to make a replacement star.

p16.text: The group returns the tin and needle and does not cut the curtain to make a star.

p17.text: Sew the brass button in the replacement star’s middle.

p18.text: The brass button is not silver-colored.

p19.text: The Moon could receive a golden-looking replacement star.

p20.text: The replacement may show better on stage.

p21.text: The replacement looks as though the friends forgot the original star.

p22.text: Nia denies they forgot the original.

p23.text: Nia says they lost the original.

p24.text: The new star’s top sags under the heavy button.

p25.text: Ben predicts the new star will flop.

p26.text: Use visible holding rather than Mouse’s pocket.

p27.text: The Moon is meant to keep the gift.

p28.text: Tuck the star into the Moon lap with the button facing the audience.

p29.text: The loop should permit lifting without dropping.

p30.text: The first test turns the button toward the wall.

p31.text: The corrected loop presents the gold button to the theatre.

p32.text: Nia endorses the corrected arrangement as working.

p33.text: Lila’s hands tremble and make Mouse’s ears quiver.

p34.text: Lila could let Nia read the line instead.

p35.text: Lila could make the scene her own.

p36.text: Mouse says he brought the Moon a little light.

p37.text: The Moon says it can see its way now.

p38.text: Nia returns the tin with the needle inside.

p39.text: The replacement star is used successfully in the final scene.

p40.text: The original is still missing, but the replacement preserves the ending.

p41.text: Lila speaks clearly as Mouse rather than retreating into a whisper.

p42.text: The final reflected light on the new star supplies a concrete ending image.
